functional_semantics.triton: y = where(x >= 0, x, 0) elementwise with a zero of x's dtype, into a fresh empty_like buffer (impl_triton.py 14-16, 33).
functional_semantics.cutile: y = where(x >= 0, x, 0) elementwise with a zero tile of x's dtype, into a fresh empty_like buffer (impl_cutile.py 24-27, 34).
functional_semantics.note: Both realise the reference torch.relu(x) (impl_torch.py 5) as a compare-and-select; they equal max(x, 0) for every finite input. Both return 0 for NaN where torch.relu propagates NaN, and may differ from the reference in the sign of a zero; neither case is exercised by the randn/randint generator (tensors.py 78-83).

stages.triton: One kernel, one launch of ceil(n / tile) programs: load, select, store (impl_triton.py 8-16, 35-45).
stages.cutile: One kernel, one launch of ceil(n / tile) CTAs: load, select, store (impl_cutile.py 21-27, 56-57).

precision.triton: Compare and select in the input dtype; no rounding introduced; output dtype equals input dtype for fp16/bf16/fp32/int8 (impl_triton.py 15-16).
precision.cutile: Compare and select in the input dtype; no rounding introduced; same dtype out (impl_cutile.py 25-27).

preprocessing.triton: n_elements = x.numel(); output = empty_like(x); x passed as-is (impl_triton.py 32-33).
preprocessing.cutile: output = empty_like(x); n_elements = x.numel(); x passed as-is (impl_cutile.py 34-35).
preprocessing.note: Only the output allocation on both sides.

mutation.triton: x is read-only; fresh output every call (impl_triton.py 14, 33).
mutation.cutile: x is read-only; fresh output every call (impl_cutile.py 24, 34).
mutation.note: Neither side mutates the input; the contract forbids mutation.

hardware_dispatch.note: Single code path on both sides.

fq_boundary.note: Both timed run() bodies read n elements once and write n elements once with no preprocessing traffic and nothing prepacked, exactly what bytes_expr counts; flops_expr counts one compare/select per element (config.yaml 14-15).
